evidence.claim: Work began in 1816 to guard against attack from British Canada.
evidence.quote: Construction had begun on the first fort at this location, an octagonal structure with 30-foot-high (9.1 m) walls, in 1816 to protect against an attack from British Canada

evidence.claim: A new survey placed the site in Canada, and builders abandoned the unnamed fortification.
evidence.quote: effectively placing the fort in Canada, all construction on this first fort stopped and the site was abandoned.

evidence.claim: The 1842 Webster–Ashburton Treaty brought Island Point into the United States, allowing construction of a second fort, Fort Montgomery, to begin in 1844.
evidence.quote: after the Webster–Ashburton Treaty of 1842 ceded strategically important Island Point, the site of the 1816 fort and the northernmost point on Lake Champlain, to the United States. Construction began on the new fortification two years later in 1844, dubbed Fort Montgomery

evidence.claim: The two forts occupied the same site.
evidence.quote: a second fortification named Fort Montgomery was built on the same site in 1844.

evidence.claim: Fort Ticonderoga controlled the carrying route between Lake George and Lake Champlain, beside the rapids of La Chute River.
evidence.quote: The site controlled a river portage alongside the mouth of the rapid La Chute River, in the 3.5 miles (5.6 km) between Lake Champlain and Lake George.

evidence.claim: The French began building the star-shaped Fort Carillon in 1755.
evidence.quote: The French decided to construct a fort here in 1755

evidence.claim: British forces took it in 1759, and troops led by Ethan Allen and Benedict Arnold captured it in May 1775.
evidence.quote: In 1759, the British returned and drove a token French garrison from the fort.

evidence.claim: After its military use ended, residents stripped out usable building materials.
evidence.quote: The United States allowed the fort to fall into ruin, and local residents stripped it of much of its usable materials.

evidence.claim: The Pell family’s restoration opened to the public in 1909.
evidence.quote: The Pell family hired English architect Alfred Bossom to restore the fort and opened it to the public in 1909 as a historic site.

evidence.claim: The powder magazine is a later reconstruction, completed in 2008 using the original plans in part.
evidence.quote: The powder magazine was destroyed by the French in 1759, but it was reconstructed in 2008 by Tonetti Associates Architects, based in part on the original 1755 plans.
